title: Code, figures, and data for the preprint "Smooth Surrogate Models Approve Impossible Firing Patterns: A Hidden Flaw in Writing Brain Codes" (Peilin (Larry) Zhong, 2026)
description: Code, figures, and data for the preprint. A smooth differentiable surrogate of a neuron's firing-rate (f-I) curve silently certifies target firing rates the real neuron cannot produce, while reporting zero optimization error. The failure is a signature of the target cell's onset bifurcation class, present in Type-II models (Hodgkin-Huxley, and Connor-Stevens in its Type-II configuration) and absent in Type-I models (Connor-Stevens Type-I and the Wang-Buzsaki hippocampal interneuron), and it is robust to sodium/potassium conductance variation. Version 1.2.0 adds the minimal-model demonstration: in the two-variable Morris-Lecar model a single parameter switch between SNIC and Andronov-Hopf onset creates or removes the low-rate gap, showing that the gap is a property of the onset bifurcation rather than of channel complexity. The failure is invariant to surrogate fit quality, and a feasibility screen against the true f-I removes it.
